prompt: Nothing looks urgent here — but scan for check anyway. Play the move that gives check.

feedback.default: That doesn't give check. Is there a rook move along a rank or file that lines up with the king?

successExplanation: Ra8+ delivers check — a move that was there the whole time, just easy to miss if you never asked the question.

prompt: The bishop on b2 looks far from the action — but scan its diagonal. Is there a capture waiting?

feedback.default: That's not the capture. Trace the bishop's whole diagonal to the far corner of the board.

successExplanation: Bxh8 wins the rook for free — a bishop's diagonal runs the full length of the board when nothing blocks it.

prompt: Black's rook just had to flee an attack from your queen and abandoned its defense of the knight on its way out. Find the move that wins the knight.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the knight. The piece that used to guard d5 is gone from the d-file now.

successExplanation: Bxd5 wins the knight for free — a hanging piece created mid-combination, not a static one.

prompt: It might look like the bishop on c8 could defend the queen on d4 — but check the color of each square before you believe it.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the queen. Check whether the bishop on c8 could ever actually reach d4, given the colors of the two squares.

successExplanation: Rxd4 wins the queen for free — the bishop on c8 is light-squared and can never defend a dark square like d4.

prompt: This position followed a trade a move ago — Black's queen just recaptured on b5. Find the knight move that forks the king and the queen.

feedback.default: That doesn't fork both pieces. Find the single square your knight can jump to that attacks the king and the queen at the same time.

successExplanation: Nc7+ forks the king and the queen — a fork that only existed because the queen had just recaptured onto a forkable square.

prompt: Two knight moves both give check and both attack a rook — but only one of them actually wins material. Find it.

feedback.default: That's a legal knight move, but check carefully whether the rook it forks is actually undefended.

successExplanation: Ne7+ forks the king and the undefended rook on c8. The other fork, Nf6+, only wins a rook defended by the bishop on d7 — check what's actually undefended before cashing in a fork.

prompt: Push the pawn forward to fork the knight and the bishop.

feedback.default: That doesn't fork both pieces. A pawn only attacks the two squares diagonally in front of it.

successExplanation: e5 forks the knight and the bishop — even the lowest-value piece on the board can win material this way.

prompt: Move the bishop to a square where it forks both rooks.

feedback.default: That doesn't fork both rooks. Look for a square with two clear diagonals, one reaching each rook.

successExplanation: Be5 forks both rooks along its two diagonals — one piece, two lines of attack.

prompt: Move the bishop onto the diagonal that pins the knight to the king.

feedback.default: That doesn't create a pin. Find the diagonal square where the bishop's line runs straight through the knight and then the king.

successExplanation: Bc6 pins the knight to the king — the knight now has zero legal moves, since any knight jump would expose the king.

prompt: The rook on d5 is pinned to the king and can't recapture. Capture the pawn it's supposedly defending.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the pawn cleanly. The rook is pinned to its own king along the d-file — check whether it can actually recapture here.

successExplanation: Bxe5 wins the pawn for free — an absolutely pinned piece can't defend anything off its own line.

prompt: Move the rook onto the file where it skewers the king and wins the rook behind it.

feedback.default: That doesn't create a skewer. Find the file the king and the enemy rook already share.

successExplanation: Ra1+ skewers the king and the rook behind it — the king must move, and the rook falls next.

prompt: Move the bishop onto the diagonal that skewers the king and the queen.

feedback.default: That doesn't set up the skewer. Find the diagonal square that lines your bishop up with both the king and the queen behind it.

successExplanation: Bb3+ skewers the king and the queen — check forces the king to move, and the queen behind it has nowhere to hide.

prompt: Move the knight to capture the bishop — notice what your rook can suddenly see once the knight is out of the way.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the bishop. Look for the knight move that captures it — then notice what opens up behind the knight.

successExplanation: Nxc7 wins the bishop, and moving the knight uncovers a discovered check from your rook.

prompt: Capture the pawn with your knight and watch what happens along the long diagonal.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the pawn. Find the knight's capture, then notice what your queen sees once the diagonal is clear.

successExplanation: Nxb5 wins the pawn, and clearing the diagonal uncovers a discovered check from your queen — a different piece than the one that moved.

prompt: The rook on d8 is defended only by the knight on f7. Capture the knight first — it's undefended and clears the way.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the defender. Find the piece that's actually guarding the rook on d8.

successExplanation: Bxf7 wins the knight for free — and that knight was the rook's only defender, so the rook falls next.

prompt: Give check to force the king away — it's the only thing defending the bishop on f7.

feedback.default: That doesn't remove the defender. The king is the bishop's only guard — find the move that forces it away.

successExplanation: Re4+ forces the king to move — wherever it goes, it can no longer guard f7, and the bishop is yours next move.

prompt: Deliver checkmate along the back rank.

feedback.default: That doesn't deliver checkmate. Find the square on the back rank where the king has no escape at all.

successExplanation: Re8 is checkmate — the king's own pawns block every escape square.

prompt: Nothing is attacking yet, but the rooks are eyeing the same open file. Give your king an escape square before you're forced to.

feedback.default: That doesn't create an escape square for your king. Push one of the pawns in front of it forward, one square.

successExplanation: Pushing any one of these pawns creates luft — an escape square for the king, before it's ever needed.

prompt: Before recapturing the knight on d5, insert this check first — it doesn't run away, but tempo does.

feedback.default: That's a legal move, but it's not the in-between move that matters here. Look for a check unrelated to d5.

successExplanation: Nh6+ is the zwischenzug — Black must answer check right now, so the knight on d5 has to wait, and the capture is still there next move.

prompt: Your knight can recapture on e5 any time — it's not going anywhere. Grab the undefended rook first.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the rook. The knight on e5 can wait — look for the undefended piece you can win right now instead.

successExplanation: Bxg5 wins the rook — grabbing the bigger, undefended prize first, before finishing the 'expected' recapture.

prompt: This move does three things at once — find it. What does moving the knight reveal, and what does it attack?

feedback.default: That doesn't combine all three. Look for the single knight square that clears the d-file for your rook while also attacking two black pieces.

successExplanation: Nb5 is a discovered check that also forks the rook on c7 and the bishop on a7 — three effects from one move.

prompt: The rook on c5 is pinned and can't recapture without exposing the king. Capture the pawn it's 'defending.'

feedback.default: That doesn't win the pawn cleanly. Remember the rook is pinned to its own king — check whether it can actually recapture here.

successExplanation: Bxd5 wins the pawn for free — a pinned piece can't defend anything off its own line.
